title: As-Salam, the Source of Peace
hook: the Source of Peace, and why the greeting goes to those you know and those you don't
tomorrow: peace on the outside. but what makes a heart feel safe?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Quddus: the Most Pure, and a bucket of water instead of shouting. Pure. Today, a word some people say all day long.

Hey. Hi. Yo. A greeting is usually just noise. As-salamu alaykum isn't: it means peace be upon you, and Peace, As-Salam, is a name of Allah. Pickthall's list in Surah al-Hashr runs: the Holy One, Peace. Then the strange detail. Someone asked the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, what in Islam is best. Bukhari records his answer, in paraphrase: feed people, and give the greeting of peace to those you know and those you don't. Why strangers? Why not just your own people?
screen: `HEY. HI. YO.` → `PEACE IS A NAME OF ALLAH.` → `TO THOSE YOU DON'T KNOW?`

segments.voice: Here's the solve. A greeting to people you know keeps a circle warm. A greeting to people you don't makes the circle bigger. And the Qur'an draws that circle as wide as it goes. In Surah al-Hujurat, Pickthall has: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Not so you'd stay apart; so you'd know one another. One human family, many tribes, and a greeting is the first step of the knowing. Peace even goes to the rude: the Qur'an describes the servants of the Beneficent as people who, when the foolish speak to them, answer: peace. So why use a name of God for hello? Scholars have read the greeting two ways at once: may the peace of Allah be on you, and may As-Salam, who is Peace, be with you. Either way, you're handing someone you've never met the safest thing you have. Something to tell a friend tonight: the answer to 'what in Islam is best?' included saying hello to strangers.
screen: `KNOWN: A WARM CIRCLE.` · `UNKNOWN: A BIGGER ONE.` · `NATIONS AND TRIBES, TO KNOW.` · `TWO READINGS OF ONE HELLO.` · then, large: `PEACE.`

segments.voice: Say it out loud, softly, three times, the way you'd say it to a face: as-salamu alaykum, peace be upon you. Each time, bring a different person to mind: someone you love, someone you barely know, someone you find hard. For the sit, stay with the last one.
screen: `OUT LOUD, THREE TIMES.` · `LOVED, BARELY KNOWN, HARD.`

segments.voice: As-Salam: the Source of Peace, a name of Allah folded into every as-salamu alaykum.
Keep this one: peace, for the people I know and the people I don't. Until next time.
